fullPassage: [1번] The Internet really is a strange and wonderful place. Information of all sorts, shapes and sizes is at our fingertips, whether through a computer, smartphone or tablet device, and we take full advantage of that. The statistics will vary depending on which article you read but the story is the same. If we are searching for product information, film reviews, travel advice or just general knowledge, the vast majority of us will turn immediately to the world wide web in the hope that it will satisfy our desire for knowledge. The result is a very revealing digital footprint of our needs. This can offer more insight about customers than any other data. When this information is fully contextualized, marketers can start to understand customer behaviours in what has become their very native digital environment. [2번] In a perfect world, consumers would pay more for good companies' products than unethical companies' product if the product were relatively homogeneous. But does this really happen? To find out, researchers conducted a series of experiments. They showed consumers the same products ― coffee and t-shirts ― but told one group the items had been made using high ethical standards and another group that low standards had been used. A control group got no information. In all of the tests, consumers were willing to pay a slight premium for the ethically made goods. But they went much further in the other direction: they would buy unethically made products only at a steep discount. What's more, consumer attitudes played a big part in shaping those results. People with high standards for corporate behavior rewarded the ethical companies with bigger premiums and punished the unethical ones with bigger discounts. [3번] Life is too short to chase unicorns. It's too precious to rely on a rabbit's foot. The real solutions we seek are almost always hiding in plain sight; unfortunately, they've usually been obscured by an unbelievable amount of fake, an astounding flood of "common sense" that turns out to be nonsense. Ever hear your boss evoke the frog-in-boiling-water metaphor? ("Toss a frog into a pot of hot water and it will jump right back out. But if you place a frog in lukewarm water and slowly raise the temperature, it will boil to death.") It's a lie ― a very complete lie. Anyone ever tell you "fish stink from the head down"? Not true. Just a fish tale that actually turns out to be fishy. You may wonder how it ever became a maxim at all. Over time, myths and mistrusts get thrown around so often they eventually feel familiar and start to sound like the truth. [4번] The upside of the Internet is that it is democratic ― anyone can say what they like ― but the downside is that there is no quality control. Far from being an electronic oracle infallibly dispensing wisdom, it contains the views not only of credentialed experts but also of uninformed idiots ― and everything in between. There is, of course, a huge amount of useful, accurate and trustworthy information online, but it is not always easy to find. Search engines like Google may help, but it is important to keep in mind that page rankings are determined by popularity rather than truth. Since conspiracy theories surrounding events such as 9/11 are popular, they are likely to appear high on such rankings, but this does not mean they are true. So if we are to avoid being misled, we need not only the ability to locate information, but also the critical thinking skills to evaluate it.

questions.passage: The Internet really is a strange and (A)[wonderful / terrible] place. questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) wonderful=훌륭한, (B) advantage=이점, (C) satisfy=충족시키다
det.analysis:
✅ ① wonderful — advantage — satisfy: 원문 일치. 인터넷이 훌륭한(wonderful) 곳이고, 충분히 활용하며(advantage), 지식 욕구를 충족(satisfy)
❌ ② terrible — advantage — satisfy: (A) terrible(끔찍한)은 wonderful(훌륭한)의 반의어로 부적절
❌ ③ wonderful — disadvantage — satisfy: (B) disadvantage(단점)는 advantage(이점)의 반의어로 부적절
❌ ④ wonderful — advantage — frustrate: (C) frustrate(좌절시키다)는 satisfy(충족시키다)의 반의어로 부적절
det.tip: a strange and wonderful place / take full advantage / satisfy our desire for knowledge

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① insight=통찰, ② decontextualized=맥락 제거된(→contextualized 맥락화된), ③ understand=이해하다, ④ native=고유한
det.analysis:
❌ ① insight: 고객에 대한 더 많은 통찰을 제공 — 문맥상 적절
✅ ② decontextualized: 원문은 contextualized(맥락화된). 정보가 완전히 맥락화될 때 마케터가 이해할 수 있다는 흐름에서 ②decontextualized(맥락이 제거된)는 부적절 ← 정답
❌ ③ understand: 고객 행동을 이해하기 시작 — 문맥상 적절
❌ ④ native: 고유한 디지털 환경 — 문맥상 적절
det.tip: fully contextualized(완전히 맥락화된 상태)일 때 마케터가 고객 행동을 이해할 수 있음

questions.passage: Life is too short to chase unicorns. It's too precious to rely on a rabbit's foot. The real solutions we seek are almost always hiding in plain sight; unfortunately, they've usually been obscured by an unbelievable amount of fake, an astounding flood of "common sense" that turns out to be nonsense. Ever hear your boss evoke the frog-in-boiling-water metaphor? ("Toss a frog into a pot of hot water and it will jump right back out. But if you place a frog in __________ water and slowly raise the temperature, it will boil to death.") It's a lie ― a very complete lie. Anyone ever tell you "fish stink from the head down"? Not true. Just a fish tale that actually turns out to be fishy. You may wonder how it ever became a maxim at all. Over time, myths and mistrusts get thrown around so often they eventually feel familiar and start to sound like the truth.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 개구리는 '미지근한(lukewarm)' 물에서 서서히 끓어 죽는다는 은유
det.analysis:
❌ ① boiling: 끓는 물은 hot water와 동일 — 이미 jump out 하는 경우
❌ ② complete: 완전한이라는 의미는 물의 온도를 표현하지 않음
❌ ③ familiar: 친숙한은 물의 온도가 아닌 감정 상태
✅ ④ lukewarm: 개구리 실험의 핵심 — 처음엔 미지근해서 개구리가 도망가지 않음
det.tip: if you place a frog in lukewarm water and slowly raise the temperature — 미지근한 물이 핵심

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 obscured와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: obscured(가려진/불분명해진) ↔ revealed(드러난/밝혀진)
det.analysis:
✅ ① revealed: 드러나다/폭로되다. obscured(가려진)의 반의어로 가장 적절
❌ ② hidden: 숨겨진. obscured와 유사 의미
❌ ③ complicated: 복잡한. 가려진/드러난과 다른 차원의 의미
❌ ④ forgotten: 잊혀진. obscured와 관련 없는 반의 관계
det.tip: obscure(가리다) ↔ reveal(드러내다) — 어휘 반의 쌍 암기 포인트

questions.passage:
(A) But if you place a frog in lukewarm water and slowly <u>raise</u> the temperature, it will boil to death.
(B) The event was organized to <u>raise</u> awareness about the dangers of misinformation.
questions.stem: 다음 두 문장에서 밑줄 친 raise의 의미로 가장 적절한 것을 각각 고르시오.

det.korean: (A) raise the temperature = 온도를 올리다, (B) raise awareness = 인식을 높이다
det.analysis:
❌ ① (A) 기르다 — (B) 올리다: (A)는 기르다가 아닌 올리다
❌ ② (A) 모금하다 — (B) 기르다: (A) raise the temperature는 모금이 아닌 온도 상승
✅ ③ (A) 올리다 — (B) 높이다/키우다: 각각 온도 상승과 인식 제고의 문맥에 정확히 부합
❌ ④ (A) 올리다 — (B) 제기하다: (B) raise awareness는 의제 제기가 아닌 인식 고취
det.tip: raise = ① 올리다(raise temperature) ② 높이다(raise awareness) ③ 기르다(raise children) — 문맥별 의미 구분 필수

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) rely=의존하다, (B) lukewarm=미지근한, (C) maxim=격언
det.analysis:
❌ ① rely — lukewarm — fiction: (C) fiction(허구)은 maxim(격언)의 반의어로 부적절
❌ ② reject — lukewarm — maxim: (A) reject(거부하다)는 rely(의존하다)의 반의어로 부적절
❌ ③ rely — boiling — maxim: (B) boiling(끓는)은 lukewarm(미지근한)의 반의어로 부적절
✅ ④ rely — lukewarm — maxim: 원문 일치. 토끼 발에 의존하고(rely), 미지근한 물에 놓고(lukewarm), 격언이 됨(maxim)
det.tip: rely on a rabbit's foot / lukewarm water / became a maxim — 지문의 세 핵심 어휘

questions.passage: The upside of the Internet is that it is ①<u>democratic</u> ― anyone can say what they like ― but the downside is that there is no ②<u>free access</u>. Far from being an electronic oracle infallibly dispensing wisdom, it contains the views not only of credentialed experts but also of uninformed idiots ― and everything in between. There is, of course, a huge amount of ③<u>useful</u>, accurate and trustworthy information online, but it is not always easy to find. Search engines like Google may help, but it is important to keep in mind that page rankings are determined by popularity rather than truth. Since conspiracy theories surrounding events such as 9/11 are popular, they are likely to appear high on such rankings, but this does not mean they are true. So if we are to avoid being ④<u>misled</u>, we need not only the ability to locate information, but also the critical thinking skills to evaluate it.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 인터넷의 단점은 '품질 관리'가 없는 것. 'free access(자유로운 접근)'는 단점이 아닌 장점으로 부적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① democratic — 원문 일치. 인터넷이 누구나 발언 가능한 민주적 특성으로 적절
✅ ② free access — 원문은 quality control(품질 관리). 인터넷의 단점은 품질 관리가 없다는 것이므로, free access(자유로운 접근)는 장점으로 단점 설명 맥락에 부적절
❌ ③ useful — 원문 일치. 유용하고 정확한 정보가 온라인에 존재한다는 맥락에 적절
❌ ④ misled — 원문 일치. 잘못 인도되는 것을 피하려면 비판적 사고가 필요하다는 맥락에 적절
det.tip: the downside is that there is no quality control(단점=품질 관리 없음). free access로 바꾸면 '장점'이 '단점'으로 제시되어 모순

det.korean: democratic = 모두에게 열린(open to all), 누구나 발언 가능한

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 정보 평가에 필요한 것 = 비판적 사고(critical thinking) 기술
det.analysis:
❌ ① locate information: 정보를 찾는 능력은 이미 'not only' 부분에 언급된 것으로, 'but also' 자리에 올 수 없음
✅ ② critical thinking: 원문의 핵심. 정보를 평가하기 위한 비판적 사고 기술

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: credentialed — popular — locate

❌ ② uncredentialed — popular — locate: (A) uncredentialed(자격 없는)는 credentialed(자격을 갖춘)의 반의어로 부적절
✅ ③ credentialed — popular — locate: 원문 일치. 자격을 갖춘(credentialed) 전문가들의 견해, 음모론이 인기 있어(popular) 높은 순위에 오름, 정보를 찾아내는(locate) 능력
❌ ④ credentialed — unpopular — locate: (B) unpopular(인기 없는)는 popular(인기 있는)의 반의어로 부적절
det.tip: credentialed experts(자격 갖춘 전문가) + popular conspiracy theories(인기 있는 음모론) + ability to locate(찾아내는 능력)

✅ ④ the critical thinking skills to evaluate it: 원문 일치. 정보를 찾는 능력(locate)만이 아니라 비판적으로 평가하는(evaluate) 능력 필요
